Dirección Nacional de Vialidad (DNV).desc: Argentina's national roads body. It is a decentralised agency that its own pages place in the orbit of the transport secretariat, within the Ministry of Economy, and it has more than 40,000 kilometres of national routes under its jurisdiction, maintained either by its own crews and equipment, by a contractor, or by a concession company. Decree 461/2025 of 7 July 2025 began a reorganisation of decentralised agencies including Vialidad, with its existing authorities carrying on their functions until new structures are approved.

Tamiz Shahar JSC.desc: A joint-stock company that handles the placement and disposal of Baku's solid household waste, and under decrees of 2021 and 2022 also the collection and disposal of waste in territories its own site describes as freed from occupation. It was created by a decree of Azerbaijan's president on 6 August 2008 and began work on 12 March 2009 after state registration; a presidential order of 22 September 2021 placed it under the management of Azerbaijan Investment Holding. Collecting and carrying Baku's household waste remains with the Baku City Executive Power.

Ministère de l'Équipement et des Transpo.desc: A Malian ministry responsible for national policy on public works and transport. Under the decree of 5 November 2002 its duties covered designing, building and maintaining roads, bridges and other structures, railways, airfields and river ports; developing land, river and air transport; topographic and cartographic work; road traffic and road safety rules; and promoting meteorology. The decree of 4 September 2012 carries no ministry of this title: the portfolios then were Equipment and Territorial Development, and Transport and Road Infrastructure.

Ghana Highway Authority.desc: Ghana's state road authority, set up as a body corporate by NRC Decree 298 in December 1974; that decree was repealed by the Ghana Highway Authority Act 1997 (Act 540), which continued the Authority in existence. It plans, develops, maintains and administers the country's trunk road network, its ferries and traffic devices, and collects tolls on that network on the government's behalf. Its own profile puts the trunk network at 15,000 kilometres; the State Interests and Governance Authority gives 13,367 kilometres, about a third of Ghana's 40,186 kilometres of road.

Belize Social Investment Fund.desc: A Belizean public body established by the Social Investment Fund Act (Chapter 43, listed as in force on 1 May 1996) as an autonomous institution and a body corporate with perpetual succession. It finances small-scale projects in social assistance, basic infrastructure and small-scale productive activities, and improvements to health and education infrastructure; its directors are appointed by the Minister for periods of up to two years. It lists its funding sources as the Government of Belize, the Caribbean Development Bank and the World Bank.

It is a body corporate made up of a mayor and six other elected members, entrusted with the general rule and good government of the town: streets, including public drains and bridges, markets and slaughterhouses, parks and open spaces, public cemeteries, garbage collection, the Town Fund, and local by-laws.

Gobierno Autónomo Municipal de El Alto.desc: The city government of El Alto, Bolivia, covering about 384.7 square kilometres and organised into 14 municipal districts, 10 urban and 4 rural. The national statistics institute projected its population at 1,109,048 for 2022, which the city's own report calls Bolivia's second most populous city after Santa Cruz de la Sierra. It is headed by an elected mayor with a municipal council of 11 elected members; basic services are a municipal competence, although water supply and sanitation are run by the public utility EPSAS, and its role in schools is providing and maintaining the buildings.

Projet de Facilitation du Commerce et du.desc: A unit set up inside the Ivorian government to run Côte d'Ivoire's part of the Abidjan-Lagos corridor programme. During preparation from 2007 to 2009 it sat under the Ministry of Transport, and between 2009 and 2012 the government assigned it to the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Its financial management specialist, procurement specialist and executive assistant were competitively recruited at the outset and its national coordinator was appointed by the government; it then had no monitoring and evaluation specialist and no social or environmental specialist.

sources.title: Implementation Completion and Results Report, Abidjan-Lagos Trade and Transport Facilitation Program APL-2 (P116323), paras 49, 54 and 59-60; cached file ICR_2019-12-18_31675125

Projet de Facilitation du Commerce et du.note: Writer blanked this as a donor-project unit with no existence outside one project. The completion report describes it: para 54 gives the ministry placements by date and the staffing at the outset. Recovered from that paragraph. UNRECONCILED CONFLICT inside the one document, left to both sides: para 49 says "The PIU which was enforced under the APL 2, is the same structure handling four other World Bank projects", naming PAMOSET, the Greater Abidjan Port-City Integration Project, the Abidjan Urban Mobility Project and PRICI, while para 59 says "Although the PIU was completely staffed and equipped, it was newly created and its staff had no experience and exposure to Bank-financed or other IFIs projects". Neither is carried on the card, because choosing between them or reconciling them by date would be a claim no document makes. No URL verified for the cached document.

Mission d’Appui à la Conduite d’Opératio.desc: A support mission for Côte d'Ivoire's municipal support programme PACOM (Programme d'Appui aux Communes), housed in the BNETD, formerly the DCGTx. It acted as secretariat to the national inter-ministerial committee that headed the programme, handled the programme's day-to-day business and centralised its information, helped town councils supervise consultants and identify and design works, and supported them on environmental impact studies and plans for resettling displaced people.

sources.title: Upgrading of Low Income Settlements: Country Assessment Report, Côte d'Ivoire
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Urban Upgrading programme

Mission d’Appui à la Conduite d’Opératio.note: Opened; the report carries every element, including "PACOM is headed by a national inter-ministerial Committee (Comite Consultatif de Gestion)" and "in which MACOM assumed the secretary-ship, sheltered in the BNEDT (formerly DCGTx)". PACOM's expansion added: the report gives it as Programme d'Appui aux Communes, not the longer name, which belongs to MACOM itself. Corrected: the writer's gloss of BNETD as "the country's national office for technical studies and development" is cut - the report gives the acronym and the former name and nothing else, and the expansion is not on the page.

Kribi Power Development Company (KPDC).desc: An electricity company in Cameroon that owns and runs the 216 megawatt gas-fired power station at Kribi and holds a generating licence for 330 megawatts; AES Sonel is the sole buyer of its output under a 20-year power purchase agreement. In the guarantee agency's 2014 record of the project it is owned 56 per cent by the power developer Globeleq, which had acquired the shares previously held by AES, and 44 per cent by the government of Cameroon.

sources.title: Kribi Power Development Corporation
sources.publisher: Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, World Bank Group

Kribi Power Development Company (KPDC).note: Opened; the 56/44 split, the 216 MW plant, the 20-year power purchase agreement, the 330 MW licence and the acquisition of AES's shares are all on the page. Corrected: "sells all its output to the national utility" - the page names AES Sonel as the sole off-taker and does not call it the national utility - and "A Cameroonian electricity company", since the page states the government's 44 per cent holding but not the company's nationality. The ownership is now tied to the date of the record rather than left as a standing "is".

Wartsila.desc: A technology and services group working in the marine and energy sectors, which spells its name Wärtsilä. It is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, and reports net sales of 6,219 million euros for 2025 and about 17,900 employees across 78 countries.

sources.title: About Wärtsilä

Corrected: "makes engines, power plants and propulsion and related services for ships and for electricity generation" is not on this page, which describes the company as a leader in technologies and services for the decarbonisation of marine and energy; the product list is cut. No nationality is asserted: the page gives a Nasdaq Helsinki listing, which is not a statement that the company is Finnish.

Siemens France.desc: A Siemens business in France. Its boilerplate names Siemens France Holding as the subsidiary of Siemens AG there, and reports that for the year ended 30 September 2021 Siemens France had revenue of 1.9 billion euros, 6,000 staff, 4 industrial sites and 23 engineering sites, 10 of them with a research and development component.

sources.title: Siemens France press release (company boilerplate)

Also corrected: "the German technology group Siemens AG" - the page calls Siemens AG an "entreprise technologique" and does not state its nationality; "working in industry, infrastructure, transport and medical technology", which is not on the page; and "from continuing operations", which the page does not say.

KEC India.desc: KEC International Limited, whose registered office is in Mumbai and which describes itself as the flagship company of India's RPG Group. Its shares are listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India. For financial year 2024-25 it reported turnover of 19,177.75 crore rupees - about 192 billion rupees - with 6,543 employees and 32,479 workers.

sources.publisher: KEC International Limited (filed with National Stock Exchange of India)

Société Nationale des Hydrocarbures (SNH.desc: Cameroon's state oil and gas company, created on 12 March 1980 to manage the state's interests in the hydrocarbons sector, with the state as its sole shareholder, and governed by the 2017 law on the general status of public enterprises. It negotiates petroleum and gas contracts, develops fields, markets the share of national hydrocarbon production that belongs to the state and passes the proceeds to the public treasury after costs. Its 2020 report puts total crude oil and natural gas sales at 784.871 million US dollars.

sources.title: Rapport annuel 2020

Société Nationale des Hydrocarbures (SNH.note: Opened. Corrected: the writer's "785 million US dollars" is the report's 784.871 million and is now exact. The national crude output figure is cut - the report gives 26.556 million barrels, not 26.6, but more to the point it is a figure for Cameroon's production, not for this company, and a national figure sitting in a company's description reads as the company's own. The 2017 public enterprises law added, since it is the governing instrument the report names. Also noted: the same report's managing director cites 38.402 million barrels of oil equivalent for total national hydrocarbon production, a different quantity from the crude figure; neither is carried.

Project Coordination Unit, Ministry of H.desc: A coordination unit attached to Cameroon's ministry for housing and urban development and placed under the project steering committee that the minister chaired, set up under the project implementation act for the Bank-financed urban and water sector development programme. It supervised the programme day to day, handled the procurement and the payments for works carried out by the municipalities, prepared the quarterly progress and annual activity reports, and was the point of contact with the lenders. Its posts were a coordinator, a civil engineer, a procurement specialist, an administrative and financial head, an accountant, a capacity-building officer, a monitoring and evaluation officer and an environmental and social monitoring officer.

It was already running the Bank-financed Emergency Economic and Social Reunification Support Project when this one was prepared, and the government used it with autonomy over the financial management and administrative capacities needed to run a project.

Bureau Central de Coordination (BCECO),.desc: A Congolese public service created by presidential decree 039/2001 of 8 August 2001 and placed under the Ministry of Finance. It manages, coordinates and carries out development projects and programmes paid for either from the state's own resources or by outside funders, in infrastructure, health, education, water and energy, as well as local development and institutional support. Its portal lists 164 projects across 26 provinces.

Secrétariat Permanent, Projet de Dévelop.desc: The permanent secretariat of the Urban Development Project in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which its own documents head with the Ministry of Urban Planning and Housing. For the Kinshasa urban development and resilience project it coordinated preparation on behalf of the city-province of Kinshasa, with an environmental safeguards specialist and a social safeguards specialist on its staff, and it approved the screening and categorisation of sub-projects during preparation; in the implementation phase that approval passes to a separate project management unit.
